name: Hydatidiform Mole

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Hydatidiform Mole

criteria.description: Characteristic 'snowstorm' or 'cluster of grapes' appearance on pelvic ultrasound
Markedly elevated serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels disproportionate to gestational age
Histological confirmation showing hydropic swelling of chorionic villi with trophoblastic proliferation
Uterine size larger than expected for gestational age
Absence of identifiable fetal parts on imaging or histology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic ultrasound findings and elevated β-hCG levels with histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by histopathology; clinical and imaging findings guide initial suspicion.

laboratory: Markedly elevated serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG)
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing 'snowstorm' or 'cluster of grapes' pattern
Absence of fetal heartbeat or parts
Ovarian theca lutein cysts on ultrasound
genetic: Complete moles typically diploid androgenetic origin (paternal genome only)
Partial moles usually triploid with two paternal and one maternal set
other: Histopathological examination showing hydropic swelling of chorionic villi and trophoblastic proliferation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of fetal parts on ultrasound
Absence of trophoblastic proliferation on histology
Malignant trophoblastic tumor with invasive growth
Histology shows absence of chorionic villi

redFlags: Rapidly increasing uterine size disproportionate to gestational age
Signs of hyperthyroidism or thyroid storm
references: Ngan HY, Seckl MJ, Berkowitz RS, et al. Update on the diagnosis and management of gestational trophoblastic disease. Int J Gynaecol Obstet. 2018;143 Suppl 2:79-85.
Goldstein DP, Berkowitz RS. Gestational trophoblastic disease: 2021 update. Gynecol Oncol. 2021;161(2):484-490.
